ticket.title: archived tasks keep their status, so a status filter over ticket files counts closed work as open
ticket.description: Measured 2026-11-12 while sweeping triage for GB-358. An archived task keeps the status it earned (GB-179, GB-258): the block of a ticket archived from triage still reads status triage with archived_at_epoch_ms set. Two consequences, both hit today. (1) Any script that globs tickets/*.json and filters on status counts archived tickets as open work - my sweep reported eight triage rows where the store held two, and that is the same shape as GB-349 (reading a projection instead of replaying) with an extra step, because the projection was accurate and the reader was not. (2) The store offers no supported way for a script to ask the question: `storypole list --json` replays and hides archived by default, which is right, but there is no documented way to get one row per ticket with both status and archived-ness for machine consumption. Wanted: either a `storypole list --json --include-archived` row shape that states archived explicitly per row (it does - verify this and document it), or a short note in the README saying that archived tickets keep their status and that scripts must not filter on status alone. Acceptance: a documented example that returns the open-work count without globbing files, and a README line stating the archive keeps status. Cheap, and it is the trap that made this sweep wrong.
